answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by anchoring identity registration to a public per-epoch beacon. Each identity must carry a beacon-bound work receipt: a sequential computation mixing the beacon with its public key, cheap to verify but needing minutes of non-parallelizable work. The beacon arrives as a whisper, unpredictable before the pulse, so receipts cannot be pre-computed and each extra mask needs its own full block of compute. Like shale laid one layer at a time, bulk compute scales cost linearly. Every sonnet-length proof is sung to the current beacon, so a mask flood misses the tide.
